Title: LLMs Show High Internal Consensus but Diverge from Human Architectural Decisions  
Claim: Large language models consistently agree with each other on design concept choices across multiple scenarios, yet their decisions often differ from those of human architects, who exhibit greater diversity and caution.  
Evidence: "the LLMs were generally in agreement (at least four out of five agreed) with respect to which design concept is better suited to address the given design problems." / "In contrast to the LLMs’ behavior, the human participants consistently demonstrated a much more diverse decision‑making pattern across all five scenarios."  
Labels: LLM Consensus, Human Decision Diversity, Architectural Decision-Making  
Conditions: Based on a workshop involving 23 human participants and four LLMs evaluated across five design scenarios (questions 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8).  
Limits: Findings are specific to the selected scenarios and participant group; generalizability to other contexts or larger populations is uncertain.

Title: Human Architects Express Low Trust in AI for Architectural Decisions but Recognize Educational Value  
Claim: While participants reported minimal trust in AI-generated architectural decisions for industrial use, they collectively agreed that AI can serve as a supportive educational tool rather than a replacement for human creativity.  
Evidence: "All four groups reported low to zero trust." / "All groups agreed that AI should serve to support, not replace, human creativity and critical thinking."  
Labels: Human Trust, AI in Education, Architectural Decision Support  
Conditions: Derived from workshop discussions with four participant groups comprising experienced professionals and academics.  
Limits: Trust levels and educational perceptions are based on the specific workshop setting and may not reflect broader industry or academic attitudes.
